Shibuya Crossing (1h free time)
All three lanes start and end at the Crossing. EAST walks out to Nanaya first and shops back; WEST is the least walking but has five stops — Onitsuka, LOFT, HUMAN MADE, atmos, MEGA Donki — so pick three; SOUTH-WEST is a single stop. HANDS sits beside the meeting point, so it works whichever lane you take.
👥 4 of you? Don't queue together — split 3 ways meet back 16:15
EAST — straight out, shop on the way back 21 min walking matcha + coffee
Crossing10 or 4 min →Nanaya or Chatei Hatou2 min →豆虎9 min →Crossing
Pick ONE: Nanaya or Chatei Hatou. They can’t both fit. Nanaya is 10 min out and sells out, so walk straight there and shop back. Chatei Hatou is only 4 min out, but one hand-pour takes 30+ min, which eats the same hour. Either way 豆虎 is on the walk back — 2 min from Nanaya, 5 min from Hatou — and you leave it by 16:05 for the 9 min back to the meet.
TAP TO SHOW ONLY THIS LANE’S STOPS ↓
WEST — the shopping lane, 5 stops 15 min walking shoes + clothes
Crossing4 min →Onitsuka Tiger2 min →LOFT2 min →HUMAN MADE2 min →atmos1 min →MEGA Donki
Least walking of the three lanes — 15 min total, because the five sit in an arc 1–2 min apart. But five shops will not fit 45 minutes: pick three. Donki here is browse-only — buy the heavy bottles tonight in Kabukicho.
TAP TO SHOW ONLY THIS LANE’S STOPS ↓
SOUTH-WEST — fastest coffee 16 min walking 1 stop
Crossing8 min →About Life Coffee
Standing bar, no seats, so it's in and out. Wrong direction from everything else — best for whoever just wants coffee.

  • 🛍 TO BUY
  • Check for Seika ZEN here. Big hair-care range and it’s the calmest place to look — if it’s in stock, buy it here rather than fighting Kabukicho at 19:15

  • But a reviewer reports the Udagawacho store is closing to become a hotel — if unsure, use Scramble Square
  • Prefer to do HANDS tonight? The Shinjuku branch works if you reorder the evening — see 19:40 today

GETTING BACK
3:45pm
Start heading back — pick one route
Hard deadline. Later than this and you miss dinner.
Route A — Toei Asakusa through-trainEASIESTHigashi-Ginza (3 min from GINZA SIX) → Keisei-Narita · ~80–90 min · ~¥1,150–1,400 · SuicaNo JR ticket needed. Some runs need a cross-platform change at Aoto — follow Google Maps live and board trains marked “Narita / Narita Airport”.
Route B — JR Sōbu Line RapidUSES THE FREE TICKETMetro or taxi to Tokyo Station → JR Narita · ~80 min · ¥1,340 if not coveredConfirm with the guide whether the tour’s free JR ticket covers this leg, and which station it’s issued for.
↳ 3:30PM, LAST STOP BEFORE ROUTE AJugetsudoKabukiza Tower 5F · till 5:30pmzero detour
Tea, teaware and a matcha parfait in a quiet room above the kabuki theatre. It’s 1 minute from the Higashi-Ginza entrance Route A leaves from — you walk past the door anyway, so save it for last rather than fitting it in early.↳ 4:00PM, ROUTE B ONLYIppodo Tea, Shin-MarunouchiSat 11am–9pmon the way
The legendary Kyoto house this itinerary otherwise never reaches — 5 min from Tokyo Station, inside Shin-Marunouchi B1. From Ginza it’d be a 23-min walk, but on Route B you’re going there regardless. ⚠ Limited to 1 matcha tin per person and the good grades sell out — don’t count on the top tier.

店Konbini Menu — what to try at each chain

7-Eleven — best food overall

FamilyMart — fried chicken king

Lawson — dessert champion

  • L-Chiki fried chicken, Machi Café latte

🥤 Drinks & October limited editions

  • Pocari Sweat / Aquarius after onsen
  • Gogo no Kōcha milk tea · strawberry milk · matcha latte
  • Chu-hai fruit cocktails (drinking age in Japan is 20 — bring passport)

写Camera & Film — best places on your route

🥇 Bic Camera Shinjuku East — the one that fits your trip

  • Day 6, ~9:15pm — 620m / 8 min from your Kabukicho hotel, open 10am–10pm
  • Full camera floors: bodies, lenses, tripods, SD cards, batteries
  • Film corner: Fujifilm & Kodak rolls, disposable QuickSnap, Instax film & cameras
  • Tax-free with passport + stack the Bic coupon (next section) — often beats Malaysia prices by a lot
  • Bonus: Uniqlo + drugstore floors in the same building

🥈 Yodobashi Camera Shinjuku West — the giant

  • Multi-building camera heaven, 9:30am–10pm · ~1km / 13 min from hotel
  • Biggest selection in Japan if Bic doesn't have your model — same Day 6 night window, just a longer walk (pick one, not both)
  • No coupons, but tax-free applies; staff let you test gear hands-on

Used & vintage cameras — honest note

  • Map Camera Shinjuku (Japan's most famous used-gear shop, superb graded condition) closes 7pm — your tour schedule never overlaps it. Only possible if you skip the Shibuya hour, which would cost you Nanaya — not worth it
  • If vintage film cameras are a serious goal, browse Map Camera's website from the hotel and note prices — everything ships internationally
  • Quick fix: Donki and Bic both sell working disposables & Instax for the retro feel

🎞 Film survival rules

  • Never put film in checked luggage — the CT scanners fog it. Hand-carry always
  • At security, film under ISO 800 survives normal carry-on X-ray fine; for ISO 800+ ask for a hand check (“firumu, hando chekku onegaishimasu”)
  • Buy rolls in Japan, shoot at home — film in Japan is cheaper and fresher than MY stock
  • Konbini sometimes stock disposables near the register if you need one mid-trip for Ginzan/Fox Village

☕ Famous must-try coffee — ranked by how well they fit

茶Matcha Powder & Tools — where to buy on your route
Heads up — the matcha boom is real: famous Uji makers (Ippodo, Marukyu Koyamaen etc.) now put per-person purchase limits on powder and sell out of top grades fast. Rule for this trip: when you see a tin you want, buy it then — don’t plan to "come back later".

🍵 Matcha powder — your 3 real chances

  • Day 6, Shibuya hour — Nanaya: Marushichi’s premium Shizuoka matcha tins, sold where you’re already buying the chocolate. Shizuoka is the "other" great tea region besides Uji — excellent quality, less hype
  • Day 7, Tsukiji hour — Uogashi Meicha (head shop): old-school Tokyo tea merchant 3 min from the stalls (Sat 8am–3pm), tastings offered, fair prices, tins + tools in one stop
  • Day 7 trade-off — Nakamura Tokichi, GINZA SIX 4F: the famous Uji house since 1854 (10:30am–7:30pm); real Uji-labelled tins + a legendary matcha parfait café — but reaching Ginza costs you Tsukiji street-food time, so only for serious matcha hunters
  • Everyday grade: Donki & supermarkets carry Itoen/Morihan cooking matcha (~¥500–900) — fine for lattes and baking, don’t pay ceremonial prices for smoothie matcha

🏷 Famous names decoded (what "Uji" means)

  • Uji (宇治) = the tea region near Kyoto, matcha’s most famous origin — a place name, not a brand
  • Marukyu Koyamaen 丸久小山園Uji, 1704not on routeFrequently ranked #1 by tea masters and connoisseurs. Deep umami with very low bitterness.Ceremonial: Tenju, Choan · daily: Aoarashi
    Ippodo 一保堂Kyoto, 1717D7 · Route BExceptional stone-ground green teas; the Ummon-no-mukashi blend is the globally celebrated one — smooth and rich.Shin-Marunouchi B1, 5 min from Tokyo Station, Sat till 9pm · limit 1 tin per person
    Nakamura Tokichi 中村藤吉Uji, 1854D7 · GINZA SIX 4FHistoric Uji merchant with exceptional ceremonial-grade powders — and the parfait.The only one physically inside your itinerary
    Tsujiri 辛利1860not on routeTraditional stone-milled teas — rich aroma, balanced rather than intense.But 辛利一本店 matcha is what your Uji-matcha Pocky is made with
    Yamamasa Koyamaen 山政小山園Ujinot on routeReliable high quality at a more affordable price — the value pick if you spot it.Often the best price-to-quality on a Japanese shelf
  • Ippodo is reachable after all — not on Day 2 (its Marunouchi shop opens 11am and your Tokyo Station window is 9:15–10:05), but on Day 7 Route B: Shin-Marunouchi B1, 5 min from Tokyo Station, open Saturday till 9pm. See the ALT PLAN.
  • Buying tips: 30–40g tin of good ceremonial grade ≈ ¥1,500–3,000 · check the grind date · sealed tins pass Malaysia customs no problem · refrigerate after opening at home

🥄 Tools to bancuh matcha (the proper set)

  • Chasen (茶筅) — bamboo whisk, the one essential; ¥1,000–2,500 for a decent 80–100 prong one (Takayama-made = the gold standard)
  • Chashaku (茶杓) — bamboo scoop, ~¥500 · Chawan (茶碗) — wide tea bowl, any you love
  • Furui — small sifter (kills clumps, the real secret to smooth matcha) · chasen holder keeps the whisk’s shape
  • Quick technique: sift 2g, add 70ml of 80° water (not boiling!), whisk fast in a "W" motion until foamy

🛒 Where to buy the tools

  • Uogashi Meicha, Tsukiji (Day 7) — chasen + scoops next to the powder, one-stop
  • HANDS Shinjuku (Times Square Bldg, till 9pm) — kitchen floor stocks full matcha tool sets; ~15 min walk from your Day 6 hotel if the night loop leaves energy
  • Nakamura Tokichi, GINZA SIX — beautiful gift-grade sets (pricier)
  • Budget hack: Daiso — ¥110–550 starter chasen & sifter; there’s one next to the A&COOP in Matsushima (Day 2) and branches all over Shinjuku. Great to test the hobby before investing

🗺 More matcha AROUND your route (verified hours)

    抹茶限购每人 1 罐，好等级会卖完。
  • 提醒：抹茶热期间名店都有每人限购 — 看到就买，别计划回头再来
    • ">
  • Kanrantei, Matsushima (Day 2) — the Date clan’s 400-year-old tea pavilion right beside Godaido & the cruise pier, 8:30–4:30pm: whisked matcha + zunda mochi over the bay. Squeeze only if the tour timing allows
  • Cha Ginza — Uogashi Meicha’s Ginza shop (Day 7 ALT PLAN) — Sat 12:00–7:00pm ✓ your window: generous free tastings of several matcha before you buy, fair prices, teaware too. Arguably the best matcha-buying experience of the trip
  • Jugetsudo, Kabukiza Tower 5F (Day 7 ALT PLAN) — serene tea shop + café by Maruyama Nori, 10:30am–5:30pm: matcha tins, teaware, and a lovely matcha parfait; 2 min from Higashi-Ginza station (your train home)
  • Ippodo Tea — Shin-Marunouchi B1 (Day 7, Route B) — the legendary 300-year Kyoto house. Sat 11am–9pm, and only 5 min from Tokyo Station, so on Route B it costs you almost nothing. Top-grade powder plus utensils; the tea room can queue ~1h, so shop-only is smarter. Limit 1 matcha tin per person and the good grades sell out.
  • Reminder: famous makers have per-person limits during the matcha boom — buy when you see it, don’t plan a return trip

関Airport & Customs Rules — Japan → Singapore → Malaysia

1 · Leaving Japan (Narita, Day 8)

  • Carry-on liquids: max 100ml per bottle in one 1L clear zip bag → Seika ZEN and any big bottles must already be in your checked bag
  • Tax-free sealed bags: keep sealed while in Japan; customs can ask to see them at departure — an opened consumables bag can mean paying the 10% tax back
  • Power banks & lithium batteries: hand-carry only, never in checked luggage
  • Royce'/chocolate with ice packs: allowed in hand-carry after security if bought airside; gel ice packs from outside may be taken at screening — buy the cold-pack version at the airport shop

2 · Transit in Singapore (2h15m)

  • You stay airside — no Singapore immigration or customs, and SG personal allowances don't apply to you
  • Changi screens carry-ons again at the gate: liquor bought at Narita airside survives only if it's in the sealed STEB bag with the receipt inside, unopened
  • Simpler trick: buy liquor at Changi during transit instead — it goes straight onto the final flight with no extra screening risk, and Changi's duty-free is cheaper anyway
  • Jewel/Rain Vortex is landside — skip it, 2h15m is not enough to exit and re-clear

3 · Arriving Malaysia (Penang)

  • Duty-free allowance: 1 litre of alcohol per adult (non-Muslim, 18+) — one bottle of sake or whisky is safe; more = declare & pay duty
  • Cigarettes: no duty-free allowance anymore in Malaysia — any amount is technically dutiable, declare if carrying
  • Other new goods: roughly RM500 exemption per person — normal souvenir hauls are fine
⚠ Meat warning: meat products (beef tongue/gyutan jerky, meat-filled snacks) need import permits and are commonly seized at Malaysian customs — eat them in Japan, don't pack them. Fresh fruit also restricted; stick to packaged sweets, chocolate, cakes, and cosmetics, which are all fine.

✈ Airport must-buys (Narita T1, after security)

  • Royce' Nama chocolate — buy last, comes with cold pack (hand-carry)
  • Japan-only KitKats — matcha, strawberry, regional flavours (great value multipacks)
  • Shiroi Koibito & Tokyo Banana — the two classic “I went to Japan” boxes
  • Duty-free Japanese whisky / sake / umeshu — remember: 1L each into Malaysia, or buy at Changi instead (see rule 2)
  • Last-minute: airport 7-Eleven for cheap snack souvenirs at city prices
礼Japan Rules & Etiquette — quick list

🚶 In public

  • Escalators: stand left in Tokyo/Tohoku, walk on the right
  • No eating while walking in shopping streets (Kawagoe, Tsukiji, Ginzan) — eat standing by the stall
  • Almost no public rubbish bins — carry a small bag for trash; konbini bins are for konbini purchases
  • Smoking only in marked areas — street smoking can be fined
  • Don't jaywalk, even on empty roads — locals wait

🚄 Trains, buses, shops

  • Phones on silent, no calls on the Shinkansen / tour bus rows near others
  • Queue at the marked lines; let people off first
  • No tipping anywhere — it confuses staff
  • Put cash on the small tray at the register, not into hands
  • Alcohol & cigarette purchase age: 20 — konbini may ask you to tap an age-confirm screen

♨️ Ryokan & onsen (4 onsen nights!)

  • Shoes off at ryokan entrances / tatami rooms — use the slippers provided, but never slippers on tatami
  • Wash & rinse fully before entering the bath; hair tied up
  • No towels in the water — fold the small one on your head
  • Tattoos: ask the front desk; many hotels have private family baths
  • Yukata: wear left side over right (right-over-left is for funerals)

🦊 Trip-specific

  • Zao Fox Village: don't crouch, don't dangle straps/phones, no touching — foxes bite; small kids carry nothing
  • Shrines (Tōshō-gū): bow at the torii, don't walk dead-centre of the path, no photos where marked
  • Shibuya Crossing: cross with the light, film while walking — don't stop mid-crossing
  • Earthquake (rare but real): drop low, cover head, follow hotel staff — don't run outside
